newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: PARLIAMENT TO PASS LAW ON DEPOSIT RESTITUTION.
newsitem.headline: PARLIAMENT TO PASS LAW ON DEPOSIT RESTITUTION.

text.p: Lithuania's parliament is expected to pass a law on Thursday to compensate individuals who lost their savings in 1990-1991, the country's finance minister said on Wednesday.
The law will compensate those who saw their savings devoured by hyper-inflation and who had their accounts confiscated by Soviet banks in the chaos surrounding the break up of the USSR.
The money will be raised through the sale of key state assets.
"We consider that around one million people will receive compesations and the total sum will amount to 3.2 billion litas," Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta told a news conference.
"The compensation will not influence the state's budget since the money will be paid from the state property privatisation fund," Shemeta added.
The chairman of parliament's finance and budget committee, Elvyra Kunevichiene, said the first payments will be made at the beginning of next year.
Citizens over the age of 80, invalids, victims of the January 13 1991 coup and political prisoners and deportees will be compensated first, she said.
"The compensation process should not last longer than three years," Shemeta said, but admitted that it will depend on success of the privatisation process.
Analysts and diplomats have questioned the move, saying that it will be extremely difficult for the government to raise the needed sum through privatisation.
